notes.meaning: Ezekiel was lying flat on the ground in awe after seeing the vision of God's glory. God addressed him as "son of man" to remind him of his humble, mortal human nature compared to the majesty of the Lord. The Lord told him to stand up so that he would be in an alert and ready posture to receive his mission.

Ezekiel did not have the strength in himself to rise after being overcome by God's holiness. As God spoke, the Holy Spirit entered him and lifted him onto his feet so he could hear clearly. Whenever God calls someone to a task, He also gives the spiritual power needed to do it.

God commissioned Ezekiel to go to the Israelites who were captives in Babylon. The Lord described them as a rebellious nation, using a word usually given to pagan peoples because Israel had turned away from God. For many generations, both the people and their ancestors had repeatedly broken God's covenant, which was His special agreement with them.

The people were shameless in their sin and had hardened their hearts against God. Even though they were stubborn, Ezekiel was sent to speak directly to them on God's behalf. He was not to share his own opinions, but to announce with divine authority, "This is what the Lord GOD says."

God told Ezekiel that the exiles might ignore him or refuse to turn from their wrong paths. The prophet's duty was simply to deliver the message faithfully, leaving the final outcome in God's hands. When the warnings came to pass, the people would have no excuse and would recognize that a true messenger from God had lived among them.

God warned Ezekiel several times not to let fear paralyze him. Serving among these rebellious people would feel like walking through painful briers or living among dangerous, stinging scorpions. Ezekiel was not to be frightened by their sharp threats or intimidated by their angry glares.

Ezekiel was told to speak only the words God gave him, without watering down the truth to please his listeners. It did not matter whether the people chose to welcome the message or completely ignore it. His sole responsibility was to remain faithful to the Lord who sent him.

God warned Ezekiel not to imitate the rebellious spirit of his fellow Israelites by shrinking back from his calling. Instead, the prophet was told to open his mouth and eat what God was about to give him. In this vision, eating meant taking God's word deep into his own heart and mind so that it became a part of who he was before he preached it to others.

Ezekiel looked up and saw a hand stretched out toward him carrying a scroll, which was an ancient book rolled around a wooden rod. The heavenly hand showed that the message came straight from God, who would also protect His prophet. This rolled document held the specific prophecies Ezekiel was appointed to proclaim.

When the scroll was unrolled, Ezekiel saw that it was completely covered with writing on both the inside and the outside. Most scrolls were written on only one side, so this showed that God's message of coming judgment was full and overflowing. The contents were heavy with sorrow, mourning, and distress because of the people's persistent rebellion against God.
